title: Pharmacy technicians in medication reconciliation at care transitions: a scoping review
subtitle: Mapping tasks, training, supervision, accuracy, outcomes and regulatory scope for a committee decision
statement: A community hospital's pharmacy technicians take admission medication histories and want to extend their role to discharge reconciliation. The pharmacy and therapeutics committee needs a map of what is known about technicians in medication reconciliation at care transitions: the tasks they perform, training and supervision models, how accuracy has been measured, the outcomes reported, and what regulators allow, with attention to rural hospitals and to pharmacists' use of time.
whoAffected: Patients discharged from medical wards, pharmacy technicians and pharmacists, prescribers who resolve discrepancies, and the committee deciding on the role.
whatHurts: Unreconciled discharge prescriptions lead to omitted, duplicated or wrong-dose medicines after discharge; pharmacists cannot reconcile every discharge; an unsafe or unlawful extension of technician roles would add risk.
currentPractice: Technicians take admission histories; pharmacists reconcile discharge prescriptions when time allows, and many discharges are not reconciled.
whyNow: The committee decides in April 2027 and needs the review by the end of March.
constraints: One pharmacist for four hours a week; a second reviewer only if the pharmacy residency director agrees to release the resident. The review must be finished by 31 March 2027 for the April committee. Library databases and interlibrary loans are available; there is no budget for translation.
patientCenteredGoal: Every patient leaves hospital with a reconciled medication list prepared by staff working within their competence and scope.
summary: Problem framed as a scoping question to inform a decision on technicians' role in discharge reconciliation.
